artists.biography: Monster Magnet is an American stoner rock band. Hailing from Red Bank, New Jersey, the group was founded by Dave Wyndorf (vocals and guitar), John McBain (guitar) and Tim Cronin (vocals and drums). The band first went by the names "Dog of Mystery", "Airport 75", "Triple Bad Acid" and "King Fuzz" before finally settling on "Monster Magnet", taken from the name of a 1960s toy made by Wham-O, which Wyndorf liked when he was a child.

perplexity.description:
Dopes to Infinity," released on March 21, 1995, is the third studio album by American rock band Monster Magnet. Known for its stoner rock foundation, the album marked a stylistic evolution from the band's earlier raw and primal sound to a more textured and sumptuous production under the guidance of frontman Dave Wyndorf. This shift challenged listeners who expected the primal energy of their previous album Superjudge, instead inviting them into a more expansive, spacey sonic journey that blends heavy psych-rock with artful sludge elements.

Within Monster Magnet's discography, Dopes to Infinity stands as a significant artistic statement, often regarded as one of their most original and ambitious works. Although it was somewhat overshadowed commercially by the later success of Powertrip, the album has gained renewed appreciation over time, particularly highlighted by the band's 2011 tour dedicated to performing its songs. Critically, it received praise for its inventive approach and rich production, earning an "A-" score from Entertainment Weekly and positive reviews for its blend of heavy riffs and psychedelic textures. Released on the Spinefarm Records and Universal Music Group labels, Dopes to Infinity remains a landmark in 1990s rock, showcasing Monster Magnet’s capacity to evolve while maintaining their core stoner rock identity.
